name: Punchcutter (open-source AI type foundry)
summary: MIT agent skill and CLI that designs real font families from a one-sentence description, a photo of handwriting or a mood image, or by remixing an OFL font (Roboto Flex, Noto, Inter...). Outputs variable and static TTF/OTF, WOFF2 with CSS and UFO sources, with spacing, kerning and its own Studio app. Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI.

access.notes: Tool is MIT; OFL remixes (route 6) ship under the OFL with a new name and the original credited.

procedure: Open https://github.com/byrishi/punchcutter and the docs at https://byrishi.github.io/punchcutter/
Install the skill in your agent (see Getting started / skills.sh)
Describe a typeface or send a photo of the handwriting sheet
Export the generated family (TTF/OTF, WOFF2+CSS, UFO)

verdict.why: Distinctive open tool that produces actual font files and sources rather than images; MIT. Young project with low adoption so far.

image.alt: Specimen of five font families made with Punchcutter: Burin Grotesk, Pomelo Round, Quarry Slab, Semaphore Condensed, Lumen Contrast
